summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (porting the node/v3 model to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack with grant-root awareness), with the user authorizing auto-advance from planning straight into unattended parallel execution.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 was planned (growing from 14 to 16 plans across two research/plan cycles) and 12/16 plans were executed and merged — the entire crates/core + crates/sdk node/v3 read/rotation/seal/emit foundation is green — but the actual FUSE cutover plan (69-09) hit three successive architectural blockers, and the session ended mid-planning of two new prerequisite plans (69-17 write-plane materialization API, 69-18 JournalOp wire-format reshape).

repo: GSD's commit helper false-negatives 'commit_failed' even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

Worktree-reported `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` can be wrong (agent reports its own last docs commit instead of the true fork point) — verify via `git merge-base <worktree-branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.

Fresh git worktrees lack `node_modules`, so husky pre-commit (lint-staged) fails on the first commit; either `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first or `--no-verify` is acceptable for pure-Rust changes.
The FUSE write path (crates/fuse) still emits legacy hex-string, user-ECIES-wrapped FolderMetadata/FileMetadata — it was never migrated to node/v3 symmetric sealing, unlike the read-listing side.

InodeKind (crates/fuse) is a read-WRITE vault-owner structure holding ipns_private_key + folder_key/file_key (needed to sign IPNS records and seal new children) — fundamentally different from the read-only web Phase 68.2 mirror, so the gated read-only listing API cannot supply what FUSE needs.

ResolvedChild (crates/sdk/src/listing.rs) carries no key material; resolve_child unseals the child read-key and immediately zeroizes it (D-09) and never touches the write-body — there is no existing API to materialize a writable tree.
crates/fuse has zero references to crates/sdk::listing; it does raw IPNS resolve+fetch at ~10 call sites instead.

Research/plan claims should be re-verified against the live tree before trusting them for atomicity decisions — the cited 'JournalOp weld' (`parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` in queue.rs) does not exist; that field actually lives in the fuse-side MkdirJournalResult struct.

crates/fuse/Cargo.toml defaults to `default=["fuse"]`, with `platform/windows/*` behind `#[cfg(feature="winfsp")]` — excluded from default `cargo check --workspace`, only checked under `--features winfsp` in the cargo-windows CI job.
The active checkout (cipher-box-phase69) is itself a linked git worktree of the main cipher-box repo — orchestrator manifest must pin `orchestrator_root` correctly for this nested-worktree case.

code.finding: JournalOp fields are all hex-string based (child_folder_key_hex, wrapped_key_hex, parent_ipns_key_hex) — no FolderMetadata/node-v3 coupling exists here, contrary to what earlier research claimed.
MkdirJournalResult (not queue.rs::JournalOp) is what actually holds `parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` — the true legacy coupling point.
Write path (mkdir/upload/delete/rename) emits legacy ECIES-wrapped FolderMetadata/FileMetadata; no node/v3 emission exists on this path.
InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} each store ipns_private_key plus folder_key/file_key — a full read-write owner state, comment notes 'Critical for write operations.'
ResolvedChild struct has only {ipns_name, name, kind, size, modified_at, sequence} — no key material, unsuitable as-is for FUSE's write-owner needs.
resolve_child unseals the child read-key then immediately zeroizes it; write-body (NodeWriteBody: ipns_private_key + write_children) is never touched.

workflow: Canary-first execution: run the first plan of a wave synchronously to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline before fanning out the rest of the wave in parallel background dispatches.
GSD role separation held even during crash recovery: spawned a fresh single-plan gsd-planner subagent to write the missing plan rather than authoring it inline.
Durable scratchpad handoff files (outside the repo, under the session tmp dir) preserved full recovery state across an explicit pause/resume and across a context-window compaction.
Dispatch worktree-isolated Agent() calls one at a time even for parallel waves, to avoid simultaneous `git worktree add` racing on `.git/config.lock`.

When a worktree agent stalls mid-stream (API error) with uncommitted changes, the orchestrator inspected, finished the last pending edit, ran tests, and committed directly from the worktree rather than re-dispatching from scratch.

Distinguished a provider/account session-limit death (zero edits made, safe to just re-dispatch after reset) from a genuine architectural halt (agent made zero edits by design after reaching a grounded blocking conclusion) — verified via worktree diff before reacting either way.
Backfilled a missing SUMMARY.md by hand (matching an existing plan's format) when an executor died before writing one, to keep GSD tracking honest.

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run on an API connection error after writing 13 of 14 plans, requiring the §9a filesystem-fallback recovery path.
GSD's commit helper repeatedly reported false 'commit_failed' results across the session even though commits landed.
Executor-reported `expected_base` was wrong more than once, requiring manual `git merge-base` verification before each merge.
cargo fmt over-reformatted unrelated files in at least two worktree runs (69-08, 69-15), requiring the executor/orchestrator to scope-check and revert drift before committing.
Two separate executor deaths on 69-09/69-16: one from a mid-stream API stall leaving uncommitted work, one from hitting the account's session usage limit mid-exploration.

The FUSE cutover (69-09) needed three successive re-scopes: first discovered the read/write path split was inseparable (~9 files + write plane never migrated), then discovered even the 'atomic' rewrite lacked a callable Node write-plane emit API and read adapter, then discovered the foundation still couldn't materialize a writable InodeKind (no key-bearing write-owner walk) — each requiring fresh research + planning cycles.

Pre-existing research/plan text was stale against the live tree (the cited JournalOp/FolderMetadata coupling didn't exist), wasting a would-be atomicity justification until manually re-verified via grep.
open_items: 69-17 (gated write-plane tree-materialization API) and 69-18 (JournalOp node/v3 wire-format reshape + replay migration) are being authored by a planner agent — not yet complete at session end.
69-09 (P1b, the atomic Unix FUSE cutover) needs to be rewritten again to depend on 69-17/69-18 once they exist.
69-10 (delete legacy crates/core types) and 69-13 (grant-gated write path + SC#2 + D-07) remain unexecuted, blocked behind 69-09.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration, TEST-03) is explicitly deferred to the user's Windows machine (autonomous: false) and untouched.
VALIDATION.md frontmatter 'draft' status warning from the plan-checker was only partially addressed.
SC#6 grep-gate in 69-06/69-09 uses a placeholder crate-private symbol name that still needs confirming against the real name at execution time.
Desktop E2E CI workflow name mismatch (ROADMAP/CONTEXT say 'CI E2E Tests', actual is 'Desktop E2E Tests') was corrected in 69-14 but may need propagating elsewhere.
Non-blocking codebase-drift check flagged 143 stale elements (mostly outside crates/) — deferred, suggested refresh via /gsd-map-codebase later.
